newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK February PSBR data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK February PSBR data.

text.p: Following is a selection of reactions to UK public sector borrowing requirement data published at 0930 GMT. The data showed a deficit of 3.58 billion sterling for February.
"It is in line. It is exactly what the markets were expecting."

"The major point about the set of data is that it confirms the public finances, in the short term at least, are in good shape and that some of the concerns raised in the market about the incoming administration and the task it has to reform the public finances is probably premature."

"The numbers are pretty much as expected. One interesting feature is the strength of income tax receipts during the month. That may well reflect the introduction of self assessment, bringing forward some income tax inflow. Overall it looks as the government is going to undershoot its forcast for the year by three to four billion sterling."

"Very much in line with forecasts, keeping government borrowing on track to meet the target announced in the November budget -- not too many surprises to upset the Chancellor during the election campaign."
